title: Part 1
text: The last chapter of a whale fall can last for a very long time, and it begins long after the chemical party ends.

title: Part 2
text: Decades pass. Eventually, the fats and sulfur compounds in the skeleton run out. The bacteria and worms, starved of fuel, slowly die off.
nxt: Yet the whale fall still shapes the deep sea, through what scientists call the reef stage.

title: Part 3
text: On the abyssal plains, hard surfaces are rare. The ground is mostly soft mud and silt.
nxt: Animals that need something solid to hold on to, such as corals, sponges, anemones, and crinoids, have very few places to settle.

title: Part 4
text: Whale falls may also matter for the climate. A whale collects a great deal of carbon in its body over a life that can last many decades.
nxt: When it sinks to the deep seafloor, that carbon is carried far from the surface and can stay buried in the deep for a very long time.

title: Part 5
text: But this ancient system was disrupted.
nxt: Industrial whaling in the twentieth century killed an estimated 2.9 million great whales, according to a 2014 study by Rocha and colleagues.

title: Part 6
text: There is a hopeful note, however. Commercial whaling was put on hold by a global moratorium that began in 1986, and some whale populations have been slowly recovering since.
nxt: As their numbers grow, more whales will die naturally and sink, and the deep seafloor may slowly see more of these ancient feasts return.
